evidence: Clear separation of concerns into distinct modules: downloader/, parser/, writer/, each with dedicated responsibilities
Shared core domain models (User, Weibo classes) used across modules, indicating tight cohesion within the monolith
No inter-process communication or network boundaries — all components import and call each other directly
Use of abstract base classes (Downloader, Parser, Writer) with concrete implementations suggests dependency inversion within a single process
Centralized control flow via spider.py and __main__.py, orchestrating the entire pipeline
Shared utilities (config_util, datetime_util) used across modules without isolation
Test suite mirrors module structure (test_downloader_async, test_parser/*), confirming internal modularity rather than service boundaries
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., parser imports downloader, writer imports parser) may reduce testability and maintainability over time
No clear boundary enforcement — modules could gradually become interdependent, eroding modularity
Single deployment unit limits scalability and independent evolution of components
